full_judgment: 3. That plaintiff's case in short is that the defendant opposite party No.1 rented a shop to the plaintiff petitioner which measuring about 240 square feet situated at Birampur Bazar of 177 Loraichar Mouza under Khatian No.126 of Sabek Dag No.372 under Faridganj Police Station taking the amount of Taka 20,000 as advanced booking and 700 Taka as rent per month applying with condition that the amount to Taka 200 would be adjusted per month with the advanced money and the rest amount of Taka 500 would be paid to the respondent opposite party as rent per month and at that instance an agreement was executed between them for a period of 5 years effective from the 1st May, 2008 up to 30th May, 2008 and the plaintiff petitioner used to pay the rent as usually and on 5-9-2008 the plaintiff petitioner paid the amount of Taka 2,000 for the rent of the period of 4 (four) months at a time, on 4-9-2009 paid the amount of Taka 6,000 as rent for the period of the month of September, 2008 upto the month of August, 2009 and on 28-11-2009 paid the amount of Taka 5,000 as rent for the period of the month of September, 2009 upto the month of August, 2010. Moreover the defendant opposite party No.1 took some goods from the shop of the petitioner equivalent to Taka 3,579 but the defendant opposite party No.1 did not repay the same rather on 7-3-2010 brought a false allegation before the Village Court with a false demand of Taka 3000 in order to evict from the shop illegally, without exercising any jurisdiction; while the plaintiff petitioner perceived that he would not get the proper justice, he brought a Miscellaneous Case being No.06 of 2010 before the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandpur for calling the records from the Village Court and after receiving the Notice the defendant opposite parties in collusion with each other prepared and Judgment on 11-4-2010 and sent the case records to the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistradte, Chandpur and on 8-6-2010 learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chadpur advised the plaintiff petitioner goes to the competent court for proper relief and kept with the record; in fact the Village Court had no jurisdiction to adjudicate the Suit No. 2 of 2010 and the defendant opposite party No.1 had the proper forum to bring Suit before the Small Causes Court in order to evict the plaintiff petitioner from the shop in question as such the Judgment dated 11-4-2010 pronounced by the Village Court in the Suit No. 2 of 2010 is illegal, collusive, beyond of jurisdiction and is not binding upon the plaintiff petitioner and hence, the plaintiffs case.
